turn1.explanation: The unit responds to the central face region (eyes, nose and muzzle) of cats, and more weakly to similar small-snouted furry faces of foxes, hamsters, red pandas, meerkats and ferrets.
turn1.evidence: Nearly all of the top 20 are frontal cat or fox-like faces, with red shading centered on the nose and muzzle; one red car front (#5) is a face-like outlier. The most negative spots are dark, flat, wrinkled dog muzzles (pugs, mastiffs) and dark blobs, which suggests the unit separates light, fine-furred, pointy feline/vulpine faces from heavy dark dog snouts.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on more dog faces with fox-like muzzles, such as spitz breeds, and on frontal faces of non-mammals would show whether the unit is specific to cats and foxes or just to light-furred small-nosed faces.
